title: Experimental latency probing for kernel pipeline
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, production-safe latency probing pipeline that produces per-architecture, per-seqlen signal to guide kernel pipeline choices with minimal disruption. The probe harness will run fast microbenchmarks in shadow mode and online sampling that target prefill vs decode phases and tokenphase/sequence-length buckets. Outputs are a compact signal store (TTL keyed by model+arch+seqbucket) consumed by the runtime routing decision to nudge kernel pick probabilities.

Motivation: current kernel routing relies on offline microbenchmarks and static heuristics, which degrade when load patterns or O/S/GPU stack behavior drift. We want a bounded-exploration probe that adapts to real traffic distributions while guaranteeing latency SLOs and stable fallbacks.

Scope and approach:
- Probe types: lightweight single-batch prefill probe, short decode-rollout probe, and multi-token occupancy sampler. Probes must be throttled to avoid capacity noise and respect per-tenant limits.
- Bucketing: seqlen buckets {<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512}, tokenphase bucketization (early/mid/late) and hardware fingerprint (arch, memory, compute capability).
- Scheduling: occupancy-aware scheduling triggered during low queue depth windows, with backoff and per-GPU quotas. Probes will run with conservative timeouts and capped concurrency.
- Safety: any probe-driven change must pass a sterilization check (latency delta predictions within safety margin) and be reversible. The runtime keeps a conservative default kernel family for each model/tier to fall back on if p95 increases by >10ms.
- Signal aggregation: maintain exponentially weighted average and variance for each (model,arch,seqbucket,phase). Store TTL = 30m by default. Include probe metadata (timestamp, occupancy, GPU util, microbenchmark stderr).
- Decision layer: a lightweight scorer computes expected latency+cost delta for candidate kernels using stored signals and selects either: stick, blend (probabilistic routing), or trial (weighted trial on a small fraction of requests). Trials are limited by regret budget per hour.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New dashboard: kernel-probe-latency-surface with p50/p95/p99 per bucket, probe success rate, probe cost (tokens*ms), and GPU util delta.
- Alerts: probe failure rate >1% in 5m, unexpected latency deviation >5% vs baseline after a rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature can be enabled via runtime flag (off by default) and rolled out to canary cluster.
- Measured p95 latency either improves or remains within -/+5% with cost delta <+5% in canary for 72h.
- No customer-facing errors attributed to probe trials; rollback within 10 minutes if SLOs violated.
- Dashboard and automated regression tests for microbench harness present in PR.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal dev cluster experiments with synthetic workload (2 weeks)
2) Canary on 1% of hosted traffic + Dedicated staging customers (2 weeks)
3) Broader gradual rollout with telemetry validation gates (4 weeks)

Risks and mitigations:
- Probe noise creating load spikes -> throttle, occupancy checks, strict per-GPU quotas.
- CUDA kernel warmup confounding latency -> include warmup runs and ignore first-sample outliers.
- Signal drift due to TTL -> adapt TTL and weight recent samples higher.

Open questions:
- Probe frequency budget for high-throughput tenants vs free-tier? PM asked for opt-out for enterprise Dedicated customers.
- Exact regret budget per GPU-hour and how to pay for probe token cost from tenant quota or platform budget.

Note: this ticket focuses on the probing and scoring pipeline. The follow-up work to wire in a learned bandit or Bayesian optimizer belongs in a second EPIC after we validate the signal quality.
acceptance_criteria: Probe harness deployed to dev cluster and produces stable per-bucket signals
Canary rollout configured and runtime flag enables probe in one cluster
Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for each seqlen/arch bucket; alerts configured
No >5% customer-facing latency regressions during 72h canary and rollback automation works
technical_decisions: Use occupancy-triggered probes rather than fixed-interval probes to reduce interference
Store aggregated EWMA signals with 30m TTL and per-bucket variance to detect instability
Start with deterministic scoring (expected latency + 0.5*stddev) before any ML-driven bandit
Trials limited by regret budget and gated by a sterilization check comparing predicted vs observed deltas

comments: 2025-01-23 - Kickoff: aligned on seqlen buckets and tokenphase. Decided to prioritize prefill probes first since they have larger variance across kernels.
2025-01-30 - Initial microbench prototype showed spurious tail latency due to CUDA context warmup. Action: add 2 warmup runs and ignore first sample in each probe session.
2025-02-05 - PM feedback (Aarti): add an enterprise opt-out flag for Dedicated clusters; also include cost attribution for probe tokens. Added to open questions.
2025-02-12 - Diego: implemented occupancy-triggered scheduler and per-GPU quotas. Observed lower probe success rate under sustained peak; tuning backlog thresholds improved yield.
2025-02-18 - Code review: PR #6734 opened. Requested changes: add more robust stderr capture and tighter timeouts on decode probes to avoid queue pileup. Addressing now.
2025-02-20 - SRE: flagged need to surface probe load to autoscaler to avoid unintended scaling during heavy probing. Added task for autoscaler hook.
notes: Keep conservative default kernel families immutable unless a validated probe suggests change
Plan a follow-up EPIC for statistical bandit-based optimizer once signal stability is validated
